campaigns.stage_basis: the company's own report of delivery

reported.title: Parnassus begins AI governance engagement with Intuit
reported.summary: Parnassus began engaging Intuit in 2023 to understand how its AI governance aligned with best practices, as Intuit built AI into tax, finance and marketing products.

reported.title: Investor group organizes human rights engagement with Nvidia
reported.summary: Parnassus joined an investor group that in September 2023 organized to strengthen Nvidia's human rights risk management, including an independent assessment of potential AI harms.

reported.title: Nvidia adds oversight, staff and first human rights assessment
reported.summary: Nvidia formed an executive-level sustainability steering committee overseeing human rights, added staff and began its first human rights impact assessment, with Parnassus input on scope.

reported.title: Intuit plans public AI governance disclosure after engagement
reported.summary: Parnassus reported that Intuit considered its requests, including stronger attention to human rights risks in AI governance, and planned public disclosure on AI governance in early 2025.

reported.title: Intuit publishes AI governance and risk management disclosure
reported.summary: Following Parnassus engagement begun in 2023, Intuit released public disclosure on its AI governance and risk management practices in the first half of 2025.

reported.title: Workday completes NIST AI RMF assessment and gets ISO 42001 accreditation
reported.summary: After Parnassus engagement on AI and workers' rights, Workday completed a third-party assessment against the NIST AI RMF and achieved ISO 42001 accreditation.

reported.title: Nvidia completes third-party human rights saliency assessment
reported.summary: The engagement prompted a third-party saliency assessment identifying five salient risks, including responsible product development and use, plus plans to strengthen human rights policies.

reported.title: Water stewardship engagement linked to AI data centers
reported.summary: Parnassus engaged Microsoft on absolute water withdrawal targets and supply chain water risk, citing AI's water and power use in data centers; initial contacts were favorable.

reported.title: Supply chain water-risk engagement as infrastructure expands
reported.summary: Parnassus reported engaging Alphabet management on supply chain water-risk reduction given the expansion of its global infrastructure footprint, which includes data centers.

commitments.engaged_by: AFL-CIO Equity Index Funds and co-filers
commitments.promised: Enhance its disclosure on its use of AI (exact terms not public).
commitments.promised_quote: According to Responsible Investor, AFL-CIO agreed to withdraw its proposal at Comcast and Disney following commitments from these companies to enhance their disclosures on their use of AI.

evidence.text: Disney's proxy for the meeting the proposal targeted already says the full Board reviews potential uses of generative AI and the development of generative AI governance principles; the 2025 proxy repeats it.
evidence.quote: The full Board also reviews reports regarding certain potential uses of generative artificial intelligence and the development of generative artificial intelligence governance principles.

evidence.text: Disney published a Responsible AI Use topic brief describing its AI principles, central review process, Board updates and three categories of AI use. Upload path is dated 2025/05; the version online is marked 'As of 5/22/26'.
evidence.quote: We have established an AI governance process pursuant to a principles-based framework and our generally applicable policies
evidence.date_note: current version; first posted 2025-05 per upload path

evidence.text: 2026 proxy lists 'Enhanced artificial intelligence oversight disclosure' among governance changes and sets out Board and committee AI oversight.
evidence.quote: Enhanced disclosure of artificial intelligence oversight by the Board and its Committees

commitments.notes: Commitment known only second-hand (FTI Consulting on the Harvard Law School Forum, citing Responsible Investor); Disney has not published the commitment's terms. Commitment date not public: it falls between SEC staff's 2024-01-03 no-action reply and Disney's 2024 definitive proxy (2024-02-01), which omits the proposal. 'Delivered' is judged against the reported promise to enhance AI disclosure; the proposal's three asks (AI use, board oversight, ethical guidelines) are each covered by the topic brief and proxies. Disney's FY2024 sustainability report not checked.

commitments.promised: Enhance its disclosure on its use of AI (exact terms not public).
commitments.promised_quote: According to Responsible Investor, AFL-CIO agreed to withdraw its proposal at Comcast and Disney following commitments from these companies to enhance their disclosures on their use of AI.

evidence.text: 2025 proxy adds AI to the Governance and Corporate Responsibility Committee's remit; the 2024 proxy has no AI governance language (checked).
evidence.quote: Reviews significant legal and regulatory compliance risks, such as privacy, AI and data governance.

evidence.text: 2026 proxy repeats the committee oversight line, now spelled out as 'artificial intelligence'.
evidence.quote: Compliance, legal and regulatory matters, including privacy, artificial intelligence and data governance

commitments.notes: Commitment known only second-hand (FTI Consulting on the Harvard Law School Forum, citing Responsible Investor); terms and date not public (filing deadline 2023-12-30; withdrawn before the 2024 proxy). Classified partial: the only company evidence found is a one-line committee-oversight disclosure. No public AI principles, AI-use report or ethical guidelines found. Looked in: 2024 DEF 14A (no AI), 2025 and 2026 DEF 14A, 2025 Impact Report (update.comcast.com/download/18245; AI mentioned only as products and training, no governance section), FY2025 10-K (AI only in risk factors), corporate.comcast.com search. The 2024 Impact Report link (update.comcast.com/download/17729) returned 404 and was not read.

commitments.promised: Publish disclosures on its policies, practices and governance for responsible AI, including efforts to reduce the risk of disproportionately affecting marginalized groups.
commitments.promised_quote: Verisk agreed to publish disclosures describing its policies, practices and governance regarding the responsible use of AI. This disclosure will include information about the company's efforts to reduce the risks of disproportionately affecting marginalized groups.

evidence.text: Verisk's 2024 Corporate Responsibility Report says it publicly issued its Commitment to Ethical and Responsible AI in 2024, covering principles, governance structure, standards and review processes.
evidence.quote: In 2024, Verisk publicly issued its Commitment to Ethical and Responsible AI
evidence.date_note: report covers 2024; exact publication date not shown

evidence.text: The Commitment document (©2024) sets 'FAITH' principles, a Board Risk Committee > ERMC > AI Governance Board structure, and monitoring for discriminatory outcomes; it cites FairCheck for insurer models.
evidence.quote: Verisk will strive to ensure that AI Systems do not treat individuals or groups unfairly.
evidence.date_note: copyright line; the copy online has file creation date 2025-07-02

evidence.text: 2025 Corporate Responsibility Report says Verisk built on the Commitment with a responsible AI course for all employees.
evidence.quote: In 2025, Verisk built on its Commitment by launching multiple AI educational resources

commitments.notes: Verisk's commitment addresses unfair and discriminatory outcomes in general terms ('unfairly biased or discriminatory outcomes'); it does not use the words 'marginalized groups'. 'Delivered' judges the publication; whether its depth satisfies Parnassus is not stated by Verisk.

commitments.ask_hint: human rights due diligence on AI products
commitments.promised: Conduct a third-party human rights saliency (impact) assessment across the value chain.
commitments.promised_quote: The engagement prompted NVIDIA to commit to conducting a human-rights saliency assessment with a third party, with full board and executive team support.

evidence.text: FY2024 report: NVIDIA had begun preparing the assessment (the company's own statement of intent).
evidence.quote: We have begun preparation for a human rights impact assessment across our value chain.

evidence.text: FY2025 report: independent firm completed the saliency assessment, naming five salient risks including responsible product development and responsible product use.
evidence.quote: In FY25, NVIDIA commissioned an independent firm to conduct a human rights saliency assessment of potential human rights impacts across our value chain.

commitments.notes: Investor group organized September 2023 (Parnassus 2025 report p.16); Parnassus 2024 report p.13 says NVIDIA was 'conducting its first human rights impact assessment'. No deadline stated. NVIDIA does not name the assessor.

commitments.ask_hint: human rights due diligence on AI products
commitments.promised: Review and update its Human Rights and Responsible Minerals policies in FY26 using the saliency assessment.
commitments.promised_quote: In FY26, we'll review and update our Human Rights and Responsible Minerals policies.

evidence.text: FY2026 report states the updates were made in FY26.
evidence.quote: These assessment results guided updates to NVIDIA's human rights and responsible minerals policies in FY26

evidence.text: Human Rights Policy now names the five salient risks and adds 'Responsible Product Development' and 'Responsible Product Use' sections (model risk management, Trustworthy AI Terms, model cards).
evidence.quote: We conducted a human rights impact assessment across our value chain, with input from both internal and external stakeholders, identifying five salient risk areas

evidence.text: Responsible Minerals Policy also shows a new revision date.

commitments.notes: Parnassus (2025 report p.16) reports the same plan: 'NVIDIA shared plans to enhance both its human rights and responsible minerals policies in the current fiscal year.' Timing caveat: both policies show 'Last updated' 2026-02-05, eleven days after FY26 ended (2026-01-25); NVIDIA's FY26 report says the updates happened in FY26. The FY2025 report date is not printed; deadline taken as FY26 year-end.

commitments.ask_hint: human rights due diligence on AI products
commitments.promised: Form an executive-level sustainability steering committee with oversight of human rights.
commitments.promised_quote: It formed an executive-level sustainability steering committee with explicit oversight of human rights throughout its business

evidence.text: FY2024 report names the Corporate Sustainability Steering Committee as responsible for the human rights program.
evidence.quote: our Corporate Sustainability Steering Committee is responsible for reviewing and ensuring the effectiveness of our human rights program.

evidence.text: FY2026 report describes the CSSC's executive membership (Legal, Finance, Operations, HR).
evidence.quote: Our CSSC is composed of members of our executive leadership team, including Legal, Finance, Operations, and Human Resources.

commitments.notes: Parnassus reports this as already done (2024 report p.13, covering to 2024-06-30), not as a forward promise. Whether the committee existed before the engagement was not checked in NVIDIA's FY2023 report.

commitments.ask_hint: human rights due diligence on AI products
commitments.promised: Add staff to support human rights work.
commitments.promised_quote: The company also planned to add staff to support this effort.
commitments.notes: Parnassus 2024 report p.13 also says NVIDIA 'has added staff resources specifically to address human rights topics'. No NVIDIA statement about human rights headcount found. Looked in: NVIDIA FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 sustainability reports (human rights and governance sections) and the Human Rights Policy (2026-02-05).

commitments.promised: Publish public disclosure on AI governance and risk management practices in early 2025.
commitments.promised_quote: In response to engaging with us, Intuit is planning for public disclosure on AI governance and risk management practices in early 2025.

evidence.text: Intuit's 'Responsible AI governance' web page describes its AI Governance Committee, risk-tiered review and NIST AI RMF alignment. Earliest Internet Archive capture found: 2025-04-15 (the closest capture to 2024-01-01).
evidence.quote: our review process is designed to identify AI use cases that require heightened review based on the level of risk.
evidence.date_note: seen by this date; archive capture; page shows no date

evidence.text: Stakeholder Impact Report 2025 sets out the AI Governance program and Board oversight, and lists the disclosure as a response to shareholder feedback.
evidence.quote: Publicly disclosing responsible AI governance structure and practices that guide how we operate and scale our AI-driven expert platform.

commitments.notes: Stated timing 'early 2025', no exact deadline. Parnassus (Sustainable Insights, 2025) says Intuit 'released public disclosure on AI governance and risk management practices in the first half of 2025'. Parnassus also says Intuit considered strengthening human rights risks in AI governance; Intuit's governance page refers to 'fundamental rights' but does not use 'human rights', so that part is not shown. Internet Archive was partly offline during the check.

commitments.promised: No forward promise reported; Parnassus reports Workday completed a third-party NIST AI RMF assessment and ISO 42001 certification after engagement.
commitments.promised_quote: Following our engagement on the topic, Workday completed a third-party assessment of its responsible AI governance framework against the National Institute of Standards in Technology AI Risk Management Framework (NIST AI RMF).

evidence.text: Workday press release announces ISO 42001 accreditation and NIST AI RMF attestation, verified by Schellman and Coalfire.
evidence.quote: These accreditations, independently verified by leading assessors Schellman and Coalfire

commitments.notes: Reported by Parnassus as an action Workday took after engagement, not as an earlier promise. Not a commitment in the usual sense: an outcome Parnassus credits to its engagement; Workday's release does not mention investors. Parnassus also 'pressed the company to commit to' a human rights policy, more responsible AI disclosure and board-level oversight; no Workday commitment on those is reported, so they are not listed here.

commitment_statuses.delivered: the company's own document shows it done
commitment_statuses.partial: part of the promise shows in the company's documents
commitment_statuses.not yet: not yet due, or due and not yet shown
commitment_statuses.missed: a stated deadline passed with no sign of it
commitment_statuses.no evidence found: nothing found either way; places checked are in the notes

field_context.title: A Look at 2026 Big Tech Shareholder Proposals
field_context.text: AI proposals at Alphabet, Amazon and Meta received 7.6% support on average in 2026, down from 9.8% in 2025 and 21.4% in 2024.
field_context.scope: Alphabet, Amazon and Meta only; Glass Lewis's own averages.

field_context.title: The Debriefing 2026: Season Review and Fall Engagement Guide
field_context.text: Total number of proposals filed in 2026 is down nearly 25% from 2025 and is at the lowest level we have seen over the past decade.
field_context.scope: All shareholder proposals, not only AI; Russell 3000, January to June 30, 2026 (page 5). The report prints no publication date.

field_context.publisher: Jill E. Fisch and Adriana Z. Robertson
field_context.title: Proxies for Politics (ECGI Law Working Paper 889/2025)
field_context.text: The authors find that the use of political-disclosure shareholder proposals over their study period, including proposals later withdrawn, is correlated with more political transparency by companies; they say they cannot demonstrate causation.
field_context.scope: Political-disclosure proposals, not AI proposals. This site's summary of the working paper's abstract.

not_recorded: Private dialogue that no party has published, AGM questions and divestments are not in these records yet; votes against directors appear only where an exempt solicitation asked for them.
